newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates slip on rise in supply.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates slip on rise in supply.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates slipped on Sunday amid a rise in supplies, and dealers said lack of buying by spinners could pull the rates lower.
They said the spinners had slowed down purchases to bring down prices, which are already under pressure from rising supplies from the main growing central province of Punjab.
"We may see prices coming dowm further if the spinners continue to buy at a slow pace," dealer Adil Nasim said.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,165 rupees ($58.41) and the MHN-93 at 2,100 rupees per maund (37.32 kg).
